title: Console guided routing authoring playbook: region, tier, and fallback variant editor
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Enable a guided, customer-facing authoring experience in the Redwood Console for composing smart routing policies that combine region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants. The feature should let customers: 1) author rules with clear building blocks (region condition, customer tier, model variant fallback), 2) validate policies against constraints and safety guardrails, 3) preview how sample requests will route (latency/cost/route hit-rate estimates), and 4) export policies to the API/YAML for automation. The goal is to reduce support tickets caused by misconfigured policies, improve confidence for non-expert users, and surface cost/latency trade-offs during authoring. This ticket covers the product spec and acceptance criteria for the MVP UI flow; design and engineering will split implementation across focused sub-tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Authoring canvas: customers can add rule blocks for 'region', 'customer tier', and 'fallback model variant' using an explicit +Add button
Guided validation: client and server validations detect incompatible conditions (e.g., region not available for selected model) and show actionable messages

Live preview sandbox: when a policy is edited, users can load up to 5 sample requests (manual or seeded) and get a simulated route decision table showing chosen region/tier/model and estimated cost + p50/p99 latency (synthetic based on model profile)
Cost & latency indicator: each rule shows a concise estimated delta (e.g., +$0.004/token, +25ms p99) derived from model metadata and region pricing
Export & apply: users can save the policy and either (a) publish to a named route in Console or (b) export policy JSON/YAML matching the public API contract
Rollback safety: publishing a policy with a global fallback (all-traffic -> lowest-tier variant) triggers a confirmation modal explaining customer impact and suggests a canary rollout
E2E tests: automated UI test covers create -> preview -> publish -> simulated traffic match and verifies server validation messages
Docs: in-console help text and a short 'how it works' modal linking to the authoring guide live in Confluence
engineering_notes: MVP server API: POST /policies/validate (returns list of issues), POST /policies/preview (accepts up to 5 sample requests and returns simulated decisions), GET /models/:id/region-matrix (model availability + cost/latency profile). Client will perform optimistic validation but must rely on server for authoritative compatibility checks. For preview latency/cost we will use existing model perf profiles (runtime metadata service) plus region pricing table. Feature gate: console.routing_guided_authoring. Backfill: ensure export format matches runtime policy schema runtime-2.1.
